extra.message: The tw_recent_order cookie value (orderRef) is concatenated directly into a SQL string executed by jdbcTemplate.queryForList(). An attacker controls the cookie, so a value such as "' OR '1'='1" allows SQL injection and full read of the orders table.

The X-Promo-Rule request header (rule) is evaluated with ognl.Ognl.getValue() on a public /storefront/widgets/quote endpoint. OGNL allows arbitrary method invocation, so this is remote code execution (expression-language injection) reachable without authentication.

renderTagline() compiles the stored vendor tagline as a FreeMarker template and processes it. Vendor taglines are supplied during (unauthenticated) vendor signup, so a merchant can inject template directives (e.g. ${...?new}) leading to server-side template injection / remote code execution.

renderBody() compiles the notification body as a FreeMarker template. Notification bodies include user-controlled text such as dispute messages (DisputeService.notifyOtherParty passes the message body here), so an attacker can inject FreeMarker directives that execute when the notification is persisted.

The tw_device_card cookie is base64-decoded into 'account|role' with no signature or integrity check, and the role string is used directly to build the authenticated MarketplacePrincipal. Anyone can forge a card (e.g. base64('x|MARKETPLACE_ADMIN')) to become an admin without credentials.

This public /storefront/session endpoint builds a device card from a caller-supplied account and hard-codes Role.MARKETPLACE_ADMIN, then sets it as the tw_device_card cookie. Combined with DeviceCardFilter it lets an unauthenticated user mint an admin session (privilege escalation).

cwe: CWE-565: Reliance on Cookies without Validation and Integrity Checking

extra.message: The tw_partner_assertion cookie is parsed with JWTParser.parse() and its claims (subject, role, scope, vendorRef, buyerRef) are trusted to build the authenticated principal, but the JWT signature is never verified. An attacker can forge an unsigned assertion JWT to authenticate as any user/role.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: readProviderAssertion() accepts an unsecured JWT (Jwts.parser().unsecured().parseClaimsJwt) with no signature verification. The resulting claims' uid is then loaded and a fully authenticated USER principal is installed, so an attacker can present an alg=none token with any uid to bypass authentication.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: ProcessBuilder("sh", "-c", ...) interpolates the caller-supplied outputFormat into a shell command string. SupportController.renderCompliance passes the tw_compliance_format cookie straight through, so shell metacharacters in that cookie yield arbitrary OS command execution.

The 'file' request parameter (fileName) is resolved directly against the compliance-docs directory without traversal checks, so values such as ../../etc/passwd allow reading arbitrary files on the host.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory (Path Traversal)

extra.message: writeReport(fileName, data) resolves an unsanitised, caller-supplied file name (AdminExportController passes the X-Report-File header) directly under baseDir and writes to it, allowing arbitrary file write outside the upload root.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory (Path Traversal)

extra.message: findColleague() concatenates the caller-supplied name into an LDAP search filter "(&(objectClass=person)(cn=" + name + "))" without escaping. A crafted name (e.g. *)(cn=*)) can alter the filter and dump all directory entries. findByTeam() at line 63-64 has the same issue.

cwe: CWE-90: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an LDAP Query (LDAP Injection)

extra.message: JSON.parseObject(bundle, Object.class, Feature.SupportAutoType) deserialises the user-supplied comparison bundle with fastjson auto-type enabled. This is the classic fastjson gadget-deserialisation vector allowing remote code execution.

OPTIONS_MAPPER is created with new ObjectMapper().enableDefaultTyping() and then used to read the user-supplied 'options' request parameter. Default typing enables polymorphic gadgets, giving remote code execution via crafted import options.

The export endpoint lets a vendor override its bound scope with the X-Vnd-Scope header (Long scope = vndScope != null ? vndScope : principal.vendorRef()), and PayoutService.exportForVendor (lines 99-111) never verifies the scope against the caller. A vendor can therefore read any other vendor's payout records.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: applyQuickFields() copies every client-supplied key onto the Product via BeanWrapper for any writable property. A vendor can set protected fields such as status=PUBLISHED (bypassing moderation), price, vendor or id. Called from VendorProductController.quickEdit and ListingAssistant.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: The X-Cb-Url header is passed directly to RestTemplate.getForEntity() with no allow-list or private-address filtering. A vendor can make the server issue requests to internal services (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/ or internal hosts), i.e. server-side request forgery.

redeliverTo() posts a payload to a caller-supplied overrideUrl with RestClient and no destination validation. AdminWebhookController.redeliver passes the X-Redeliver-To header straight in, allowing SSRF to arbitrary internal endpoints.

CORS is configured with setAllowedOriginPatterns(List.of("*")) together with setAllowCredentials(true) for /vendor/** and /support/**. This reflects any Origin and permits credentialed cross-origin reads, exposing authenticated vendor/support data to malicious sites.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: The filter removes the X-Frame-Options header whenever the request carries a storefront_embed cookie. Any attacker-controlled page can set that cookie and frame authenticated storefront pages, defeating clickjacking protection.

cwe: CWE-1021: Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers or Frames

extra.message: OperatorBootstrap provisions a MARKETPLACE_ADMIN account at startup using a hard-coded default passphrase (Tradewind#Ops2024, also present in operator-welcome.json). The credential is public in the repo and grants full admin access on any deployment where the resource is present.

The one-time sign-in code is generated with a non-cryptographic java.util.Random (SIGN_IN_CODE) at line 356 (nextInt). Its output is predictable and the code can be used in the password reset flow, weakening the sign-in/reset security.

cwe: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator
CWE-330: Use of Insufficiently Random Values

extra.message: Passwords imported from the legacy platform are stored and verified as an unsalted MD5 digest (DigestUtils.md5DigestAsHex in importLegacyUser line 270 and matchesImportedDigest), and legacy partner credentials use PBKDF2WithHmacSHA1 with only 1024 rounds (lines 300-317). MD5/weak KDF makes offline cracking of the credential store feasible.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort
CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm

extra.message: safeMediaType() explicitly allows image/svg+xml to be served inline. Uploaded SVG files (an allowed upload type) can contain embedded <script>, so navigating directly to a downloaded SVG executes JavaScript in the marketplace origin (stored XSS). See also SharedInfrastructureController.mediaTypeFor which serves .svg as image/svg+xml.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (XSS)

extra.message: redirectBackWithError() takes the raw Referer header and uses it as the redirect target with no same-site validation. An attacker can lure a user from a crafted page to an endpoint that raises a domain error, causing the browser to be redirected to the attacker's URL (open redirect).

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site (Open Redirect)

extra.message: The mailer writes the recipient, subject and body to the application log. Bodies include password-reset and invite links (and sign-in codes) produced by AuthController, exposing sensitive tokens to anyone with log access.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File
